The Telangana State Road Transport ... vs Algot Ganesh on 18

 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 M.A.C.M.A.No.599 of 2023
Judgment:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This appeal is preferred by the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation questioning the order and decree, dated 10.08.2022 passed in M.V.O.P.No.284 of 2018 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge at Nizamabad (for short, the Tribunal).
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge at Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties have been referred to as arrayed before the Tribunal.
3. The claimant filed the above M.V.O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident.

It is stated that on 06.05.2018 at about 19:00 hours, while the claimant was proceeding towards his shop on his motorcycle bearing No.TS-16-EP-2720, and when he reached in front of BSNL office, near RTC Bus Stand, RP Road, Nizamabad, one RTC Bus bearing No.TS-16-0193 came from his behind driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the Traffic Constable Booth and then dashed the motorcycle of the claimant, due to which, the claimant fell down and sustained fracture of spinal cord, traumatic SC I-L1, fracture of E-crd compression SX L1 laminectomy and d-12-L2,
injuries on both hands, both legs and multiple and grievous injuries all over the body.

It is stated that immediately after the accident, the claimant was shifted to Government General Hospital,
Nizamabad, and then shifted to Bombay Nursing Home, Nizamabad, and from there, he was shifted to Yashoda Hospital, Hyderabad, where the petitioner underwent treatment as inpatient from 07.05.2018 to 11.05.2018.
It is further stated that by the time of accident, the petitioner was doing and business and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Basing on the complaint given by the petitioner, the Police, I Town Police Station, Nizamabad, registered a case in Crime No.118 of 2018 for the offence under Section 337 IPC.
The petitioner filed the aforesaid M.V.O.P. against the TSRTC claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him.
4. Before the Tribunal, the TSRTC filed a counter denying the averments of the claim petition and contended that the amount claimed is excessive and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues for trial:
1) Whether the petitioner received injuries in the motor accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the TSRTC Bus bearing No.TS-16-0193 by its driver?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
If so, to what extent and from whom?

sentences.text: During trial, on behalf of the claimant, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A12 were marked.
On behalf of the TSRTC, R.W.1 was examined, but no documents were marked.

7. After considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the RTC bus and awarded total compensation of Rs.10,32,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum.
Aggrieved by the said order, the T.S.R.T.C. filed the present appeal.

8. Heard Sri Thoom Srinivas, the learned Standing Counsel for T.S.R.T.C appearing for the petitioner and Sri Azar Sravan Kumar, the learned counsel for the respondent and perused the record.
9.

During the course of hearing of appeal, learned counsel for appellant submitted that the Tribunal erred in awarding a sum of Rs.10,32,000/- towards compensation without there being any acceptable evidence on record, that the Tribunal failed to appreciate the issue as to whether there is any contributory negligence on part of the claimant/injured.
He further submitted that Tribunal erred in considering the income of the claimant as Rs.11,000/- per annum by adding 10% towards future prospects without any proof to that effect.

He further submitted that the Tribunnal erred in awarding the amounts towards pain and suffering, future earnings and so also interest and finally,
prayed to set aside the award passed by the Tribunal.

10. Learned counsel for respondent submitted that on due consideration of the evidence and material placed on record, the Tribunal had rightly awarded the amount and therefore, there is no need to interfere with the award of the Tribunal and prayed to dismiss the appeal.

Consideration:
11. With regard to the injuries sustained by the injuries, on behalf of respondent/claimant,

P.W.2-Dr.Jhansi Laxmi was examined and she deposed that as per Ex.A3-injury certificate,
respondent admitted in their hospital on 07.05.2018 with fracture injuries and he was treated by Dr.K.Sanjay and they found paraplegia secondary to B-12-L1 fracture dislocation and planned for surgery laminoctory and B-12-L2 fixation under general anesthesia and was discharged on 11.05.2018.
They issued Ex.A3-medical certificate, Ex.A5-discharge card Ex.A6- discharge advise prescription, Ex.A7-final bill issued by their hospital, Ex.A9-medical bills and Ex.C1-admission card.
She further stated that due to above injuries, the claimant cannot walk and require an attendant for his routine work and has to move around with the help of wheel chair for life long.

12. On evaluation of the evidence, P.W.1, who is the respondent/claimant and P.W.2, who is the Doctor and also the documents placed before the Tribunal, the Tribunal MACT awarded the following amounts under various heads:
i) Loss of earnings:

sentences.text: The Tribunal considered the monthly earnings of the claimant at Rs.10,000/- from paddy business, basing on the income tax returns filed by the claimant for the assessment years 2014-15 to 2016-17, wherein, his annual income was shown as Rs.3,52,150/- to Rs.5,09,985/-.

ii) Pain, suffering and trauma:
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant i.e., multiple grievous injuries and also post traumatic sequel-limbs, post traumatic sequel-spine and 90%
disability to his bilateral lower limb, spine, impaired reach and further, the statement of P.W.2 that the claimant has to move only on wheel chair for life long, the Tribunal had awarded reasonable amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain, suffering and trauma.
iii) Medical expenses:
The Tribunal had considered Ex.A6-prescriptions numbering three, Ex.A7-hospital bill for Rs.2,15,398/- and Ex.A8-medical bills for an amount of Rs.41,983/-, and awarded a sum of Rs.2,58,000/-.
Further, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards transportation and extra nourishment.

As claimant received fracture injuries and would not attend his duties for three months, he was awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of earnings and further awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- towards attendant charges for three months @ Rs.10,000/- per month considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant.
iv) Loss of future earnings on account of disability:

As per the evidence of P.W.2, claimant requires an attendant for his routine work and will move with the help of wheel chair for his long life, and as per Ex.A11-disability certificate, by which the Medical Board, Nizamabad assessed the disability as post traumatic sequel-limbs, post traumatic sequel spine and cause of disability is due to accident and percentage of disability is assessed as 90%.

The Tribunal held that claimant suffered with permanent disability not less than 50% for his spine surgery and taking into consideration of the same and as petitioner was aged about 56 years as on the date of accident, by applying multiplier '9', awarded an amount of Rs.5,94,000/-.
13.

In the light of above discussion, evidence and material placed on record, in considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal passed a well reasoned order by taking into consideration all the aspects i.e.,
the disability sustained by the claimant, nature of treatment undergone by him, medical expenses and pain, suffering and trauma and thereby rightly awarded an amount of Rs.10,32,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum.

sentences.text:
Conclusion:
14.
In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the considered view that appellant failed to make out any case warranting interference by this Court with the impugned award.
Accordingly, the Appeal is dismissed, confirming the impugned order and decree passed by the Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY,J Date:
